senses.sense_definition: A teacher of rhetoric, philosophy, and politics in ancient Greece.

examples.text: The <w>sophist</w> traveled from city to city to teach young men the art of public speaking.
Many students in Athens sought out a famous <w>sophist</w> to improve their political influence.

senses.sense_definition: A person who uses clever but false or misleading arguments.

examples.text: The politician was dismissed as a mere <w>sophist</w> who cared more about winning debates than finding the truth.
Do not trust the <w>sophist</w> when he tries to justify his dishonest actions with complex logic.

senses.sense_definition: A person who is deceptive or overly critical in their arguments.

examples.text: The <w>sophist</w> twisted every word to make his opponent look foolish during the public hearing.
Only a <w>sophist</w> would ignore the clear evidence to support such a ridiculous claim.

senses.sense_definition: An alternative form of <w>sophister</w>, referring to a university student who has completed at least one year.

examples.text: In the old university system, a <w>sophist</w> was expected to demonstrate advanced knowledge of logic.
The young <w>sophist</w> spent his second year studying classical texts in the library.

traits.comment: Refers to an older academic term.
